Additional income: $14,600 (data analysis, 2 clients), $2,340 from Synchrony Bank, $440 from Robinhood. Home office: 110 sq ft exclusive; I pay $1,600/month for 780 sq ft. steps.agent_response:
Here is a breakdown of how to handle your tax situation for the 2024 tax year based on the details provided. 

***Disclaimer:** I am an AI assistant, not a CPA or tax professional. The following is for informational purposes based on 2024 IRS tax rules. You should consult a qualified tax advisor or use certified tax software to file your return.*

### 1. Standard Deduction vs. Itemizing
**Recommendation: Take the Standard Deduction.**
*   For 2024, the Standard Deduction for Married Filing Jointly (MFJ) is **$29,200**.
*   To itemize, your total eligible deductions (charitable gifts, state/local taxes up to $10,000, mortgage interest, etc.) would need to exceed $29,200. 
*   Your known itemized deductions are only $1,100 (United Way). Even factoring in Arizona state income taxes, you will fall far short of $29,200. Taking the standard deduction will save you much more money.

### 2. What You Can Deduct (and How)
Even if you take the Standard Deduction, you can still claim "above-the-line" deductions and business expenses:

*   **Student Loan Interest:** You can deduct up to **$2,500** of the $4,400 you paid. This is an adjustment to income (above-the-line), meaning you get this deduction *in addition* to the standard deduction. (Your joint income is well below the phase-out limit, which starts at $165,000 for MFJ in 2024).
*   **Charitable Contributions ($1,100):** Because you are taking the standard deduction, you generally cannot deduct this charitable contribution (the temporary pandemic-era rule allowing non-itemizers to deduct charity has expired).
*   **Unreimbursed Expenses ($950):** 
    *   *If these were for your W-2 job (Acme Corp):* You **cannot** deduct them. The Tax Cuts and Jobs Act eliminated unreimbursed employee expenses for W-2 workers.
    *   *If these were for your freelance/data analysis work:* You **can** deduct the full $950 as a business expense on your Schedule C.

### 3. How to Treat the Home Office
Because you have self-employment income (the $14,600 from data analysis), you can take a home office deduction against that specific income, provided the space is used *exclusively and regularly* for your freelance business. 

You have two ways to calculate this:
*   **Simplified Method:** 110 sq ft × $5 per sq ft = **$550 deduction**.
*   **Actual Expenses Method:** Your office is 14.1% of your home (110 sq ft / 780 sq ft). You pay $19,200/year in rent ($1,600 × 12). 14.1% of your annual rent is **$2,707.20**. You can also add 14.1% of your utilities and renter's insurance.

**Recommendation:** Use the **Actual Expenses Method**, as it provides a significantly higher deduction (~$2,707 vs $550), which will lower both your income tax and your self-employment tax.

### 4. Forms You Will Need
When you file, your return will consist of the main Form 1040 plus several schedules:
*   **Form 1040:** The main tax return document.
*   **Schedule 1 (Additional Income and Adjustments):** To report your business income and claim your $2,500 student loan interest deduction.
*   **Schedule 2 (Additional Taxes):** To calculate the self-employment tax on your freelance income.
*   **Schedule B (Interest and Ordinary Dividends):** Required because your combined interest ($2,340) and dividends ($440) exceed $1,500.
*   **Schedule C (Profit or Loss from Business):** To report your $14,600 freelance income and deduct your home office and (if applicable) the $950 in unreimbursed business expenses.
*   **Schedule SE (Self-Employment Tax):** To calculate the Social Security and Medicare taxes owed on your net freelance profit.
*   **Form 8829 (Expenses for Business Use of Your Home):** Required if you choose the Actual Expenses method for your home office. 

*Note: Don't forget to file your Arizona state tax return as well, which will pull most of its starting figures directly from your federal return.*

### 1. Standard vs. Itemized Deductions

*   For 2024, the Standard Deduction for Married Filing Jointly is **$29,200**.

### 2. What is Deductible? (Above-the-Line & Business Deductions)
Even though you are taking the standard deduction, you can still claim "above-the-line" deductions and business expenses:
*   **Student Loan Interest:** You paid $4,400, but the IRS caps the student loan interest deduction at **$2,500** per year. Based on your combined income (roughly $100k), you are well below the phase-out limit for married couples ($165,000–$195,000), so you can deduct the full $2,500.
*   **Work Supplies ($720):**

### 3. How to Handle the Home Office
Because you have self-employment income (the 1099 data analysis), you can claim the home office deduction against that income, provided the office is used *exclusively and regularly* for your freelance work. You have two ways to calculate this:
